claim: The proteome-wide thermal shift assay has emerged as a powerful tool for interrogating compound mechanism of action.
source: Owing to its ability to approximate compound-dependent changes in thermal stability, the proteome-wide thermal shift assay has emerged as a powerful tool in this arsenal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general assertion about the utility of the method.

claim: The study quantified more than one million thermal stability measurements in response to 96 compounds in living cells and 70 compounds in lysates.
source: Taking advantage of this advance, we quantified more than one million thermal stability measurements in response to multiple classes of therapeutic and tool compounds (96 compounds in living cells and 70 compounds in lysates).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of measurements and compounds tested.

claim: Approximately 80% of compounds with quantifiable targets caused a significant change in the thermal stability of an annotated target.
source: When interrogating the dataset as a whole, approximately 80% of compounds (with quantifiable targets) caused a significant change in the thermal stability of an annotated target.
evidence: The abstract provides this percentage as a summary finding from the dataset.

claim: There was evidence of off-target engagement despite extensive use of the compounds in the laboratory and/or clinic.
source: There was also a wealth of evidence portending off-target engagement despite the extensive use of the compounds in the laboratory and/or clinic.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study.

claim: The combined application of cell- and lysate-based assays aided in the classification of primary (direct ligand binding) and secondary (indirect) changes in thermal stability.
source: Finally, the combined application of cell- and lysate-based assays, aided in the classification of primary (direct ligand binding) and secondary (indirect) changes in thermal stability.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a methodological advantage.

claim: Mass spectrometry has emerged as a powerful tool for interrogating compound mechanism of action by aiding in the validation of known targets and the identification of new ones.
source: Because of its unique ability to probe cell function on a proteome-wide scale, mass spectrometry (MS) has emerged as a powerful tool for interrogating compound mechanism of action by aiding in the validation of known targets and the identification of new ones (Moellering and Cravatt, 2012; Daub, 2015; Schürmann et al., 2016; Frantzi et al., 2019; Robers et al., 2020; Kuljanin et al., 2021; Meissner et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: All proteins have a characteristic melting temperature that can be influenced by ligand-binding, protein-protein interactions, and PTMs.
source: All proteins have a characteristic melting temperature, and this physical property can be influenced by numerous factors (ligand-binding, protein-protein interactions, and PTMs) that make a given protein more or less resistant to thermal denaturation (Koshland, 1958).
evidence: This is a general statement about protein biophysics supported by a citation.

claim: PISA uses TMT-based quantitative proteomics to estimate the area under a protein melting curve.
source: Rather than building complete melting curves, PISA uses TMT-based quantitative proteomics to estimate, or integrate, the area under a protein melting curve (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes the PISA method and references a figure that illustrates it.

claim: PISA measures a change in solubility (∆SM) rather than a change in melting temperature (∆TM).
source: Instead of TMT labelling the soluble fraction from each individual temperature—as in CETSA and TPP—PISA pools the soluble fractions of multiple samples heated across a thermal gradient such that a single TMT reporter represents an entire integrated melting curve. So, while CETSA and TPP measure a change in melting temperature (∆TM), PISA measures a change in solubility (∆SM).
evidence: The text explicitly contrasts PISA with CETSA and TPP.

claim: There is a strong correlation between ∆TM and ∆SM, making PISA a reliable surrogate for measuring direct changes in protein thermal stability.
source: Critically, there is a strong correlation between ∆TM and ∆SM, which makes PISA a reliable, if still imperfect, surrogate for measuring direct changes in protein thermal stability (Gaetani et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: PISA results in an eightfold theoretical improvement in throughput compared to TPP and CETSA.
source: Owing to improved scalability, PISA results in an eightfold theoretical improvement in throughput compared to TPP and CETSA.
evidence: The text explicitly states this throughput advantage.

claim: K562 cells were chosen because they grow in suspension, have been frequently used in similar studies, and can easily be transferred to PCR tubes for thermal melting.
source: We chose K562 cells, which grow in suspension, because they have been frequently used in similar studies and can easily be transferred from a culture flask to PCR tubes for thermal melting (Savitski et al., 2014; Jarzab et al., 2020).
evidence: The text provides reasons for the cell line choice with citations.

claim: A temperature range of 48–58°C was selected for the PISA experiments, which encompasses the back half of most protein melting curves in K562 cells.
source: After testing a number of ranges experimentally, we ultimately settled on a temperature range of 48–58°C, which encompasses the back half of most protein melting curves in K562 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Jarzab et al., 2020).
evidence: The text states the temperature range and references a figure and citation.

claim: Treatment of K562 cells with CDK4/6 inhibitors (ribociclib, abemaciclib, and palbociclib) caused a statistically significant change in CDK4 and CDK6 thermal stability when using the 48–58°C thermal window.
source: In cells heated across the full melting curve, CDK4 and CDK6 experienced minimal log2 fold changes, whereas utilizing the narrower range yielded a statistically significant change in CDK4 and CDK6 abundance following thermal denaturation and centrifugation, which, in a PISA experiment, is consistent with a ligand-induced thermal shift or, more specifically, a thermal stabilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text describes the experimental result and references a figure.

claim: Each of the three CDK4/6 inhibitors appears to engage a unique set of kinases.
source: In fact, each of the three CDK4/6 inhibitors appear to engage a unique set of kinases, which might contribute to their disparate clinical and molecular phenotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G; Hafner et al., 2019).

claim: Inhibition of CDK4/6 prevents phosphorylation of RB1, inducing a change in its thermal stability.
source: Finally, we observed a consistent inhibitor-induced negative log2 fold change in soluble protein abundance for RB1, a well-established phosphorylation target of CDK4/6, which is consistent with a thermal destabilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F; Narasimha et al., 2014). The simplest explanation of this change is that inhibition of CDK4/6 prevents phosphorylation of RB1 thereby inducing a change in its thermal stability.
